chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a traveler who stays with some of his family for a day or a night. He said: He shortens the salat (prayer).

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the salat (prayer), specifically the obligatory prayer affected by travel
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: the traveler, a person under the legal ruling of travel
key_terms.بَعْضِ أَهْلِهِ: some of his family or relatives
key_terms.يَوْمًا أَوْ لَيْلَةً: for a day or for a night, indicating a short duration
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: he shortens, meaning he performs the shortened form

ai.seo_question: Does a traveler shorten salat (prayer) if he stays one day or one night with some of his family?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a traveler who stops with some of his family for a day or a night. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rules that such a person still shortens the salat (prayer), indicating that a brief stay with relatives does not by itself change the ruling of travel.
